afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 152346
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
446 PM MST Sun Nov 15 2026

.UPDATE...00Z Aviation Discussion.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...

- A period of tranquil weather and warming temperatures will 
  carry us into the beginning of the work week.

- Unsettled weather will return Tuesday and again late in the 
  week, leading to a couple periods with rain chances over 
  portions of Arizona, and cooling temperatures near to below 
  daily normals. 

&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
Midlevel water vapor imagery depicts a transient, shorter 
wavelength ridge translating eastward ahead of a potent upper low 
that is diving southeastward from off the Pacific Northwest Coast.
The axis of this shortwave ridge is situated almost directly 
overhead at this hour, leading to a temporary peak in H5 heights 
aloft, currently analyzed near or just in excess of 580 dam. Lower
level thermal profiles have responded quickly to the increasing 
heights aloft, resulting in warming temperatures. Temperatures 
have already reached the middle to upper 70s across the typically 
warmer lower desert locales this afternoon. These temperatures are
very near the daily normals for mid November. Tranquil conditions
will prevail into Monday, and under ensemble mean 850 mb 
temperatures peaking between 11C-15C, afternoon highs should warm 
a few degrees further to around 80F across the typically warmer 
lower desert locales on Monday. This high temperature forecast may
be complicated by increasing high clouds ahead of the next 
weather system which will begin to impinge on the region Monday 
night, particularly over the western deserts, so NBM highs may 
overperform across portions of Southeast CA and Southwest AZ. 
Regardless, Monday is shaping up to be the warmest day of the next
week as a series of weather systems act to advect cooler 
airmasses into the area Tuesday onward. 

&&

.LONG TERM /TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...    
Ensembles remain in good agreement that longwave troughing will 
be maintained off the West Coast through the upcoming work week 
into next weekend, as a series of potent upper lows (centers of 
strongly negative midlevel height anomalies) dive 
south/southeastward from the Gulf of Alaska and fill out the base 
of the longwave trough. These systems are then advertised to eject
eastward over the Western US, albeit in a weakening phase as they
progress inland. The first of these systems is still shown moving
through the region Monday night through Tuesday night, dragging 
the southern extent of a cold front over the forecast area during 
the day on Tuesday. Ascent mechanisms ahead of the low will be 
sufficient to produce at least scattered shower activity and may 
release modest elevated instability up to around 100-250 J/kg, 
resulting in low chances for isolated/embedded convection 
(lightning). GFS deterministic guidance does show some weak 
frontogenetic forcing present as well, which could serve as a 
focus for a band of showers/embedded convective activity Tuesday 
afternoon across a portion of Southern and Central AZ. Latest 
WPC/NBM QPF has come down from previous forecasts, though it is 
tough to say if this is a trend or just model variation. 
Regardless, NBM 25th-75th percentiles for Phoenix are now between
0.05"-0.50", with rain totals most likely averaging 0.10"-0.25" 
and higher totals focused over foothills and south/southwest 
facing slopes to the north and northeast of Phoenix. 
Embedded/isolated convection could produce locally higher totals. 

In addition to the rain chances, Tuesday's system will result in 
decent height packing and thus fairly widespread breezy 
conditions. The terrain gap along I-8 in far southwest Imperial 
County will be most susceptible strong winds, with gusts likely 
exceeding 40-55 mph, and so a Wind Advisory may be needed in 
future updates. 

Conditions will quickly dry on the backside of this first system,
with ensemble mean PWATs dropping closer to seasonal averages 
(0.40-0.50"). Another transient ridge will likely take hold and 
allow temperatures to moderate closer to normal before another 
Pacific low impinges on the Southwest US late in the week. Model 
consensus remains that this next system will have a track further 
to the north, and thus PoPs and QPF remain fairly low and confined
mostly to AZ higher terrain areas, however, discrepancies in 
timing are still apparent, and the track is not certain. The 
temperature forecast has come into better agreement late week into
next weekend, with NBM IQRs now below 5F. Forecast highs drop 
into a middle 60s to middle 70s range across the lower deserts 
late week into next weekend, at least a few degrees below daily 
normals. 

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 2345Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT:
No aviation weather concerns will exist through the forecast
period. Winds will remain light out of the E-SE, generally aob 7
kt, with extended periods of variability and nearly calm
conditions. A westerly shift is not anticipated at KPHX this
evening. Any lingering low clouds will continue to lift and
scatter out this evening. Skies will be mostly clear overnight 
before FEW-SCT high clouds move into the region tomorrow morning.

Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:
No aviation weather concerns will exist through the forecast
period. Winds will favor a westerly direction at KIPL and a
northerly direction at KBLH tonight. Speeds will generally remain
around 7 kts or less. FEW-SCT, and at times BKN, low level clouds
with bases aoa 6-8 kft will persist with additional high clouds
moving into SE California early tomorrow morning.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER... 
Dry conditions and temperatures warming near to slightly above 
normal will prevail into the beginning of the week before another
weather system moves through the region on Tuesday, bringing 
30-70% chances for wetting rain across primarily the higher
terrain of the eastern districts. Afternoon minimum humidities 
will continue to range between 30-60% areawide through the week, 
following good to excellent overnight recovery. Widespread breezy 
and locally windy conditions in Southeast CA will develop with the
next system on Tuesday. This system will also cool temperatures 
back into a below normal category. A second weather system will 
likely reach the area by Friday and result in even cooler 
temperatures and another round of rain chances. 

&&

.HYDROLOGY...
Gila: A Flood Warning remains in effect from Painted Rock Dam 
through the Dateland area through at least early next week due to 
water released from the dam. Water releases remain at 3000 cfs and 
are expected to remain at this level through the next several days. 
This will have the potential to flood farm fields and low water 
crossings along the river downstream from the dam.

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...None.
CA...None.
&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Whittock
LONG TERM...Whittock
AVIATION...Salerno
FIRE WEATHER...Whittock/Ryan 
HYDROLOGY...Lojero
